Definition: Integration of farmer registries, agricultural input vouchers, land registrations, extension services data
Comments: No evidence found of farmer registries or agricultural input systems integrated with any data exchange platform. Agriculture is mentioned as a beneficiary sector in the Masterplan but no specific interoperability plans are detailed.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) understated available evidence: Gambia has several standalone agricultural digitisation systems (the Gambia National Agricultural Database/Ag M&E system, an AfDB-funded Farm Digitalisation and Registry project, tablet-based farmer registration under the Rice Value Chain Transformation Project, and a World Bank-funded GIRAV e-extension platform), but none is documented as integrated with a cross-government data exchange or interoperability layer, and no such national platform is yet operational. Recoded to 1 (Not integrated) on the basis of positive evidence of non-integration rather than an absence of information.
revised_comments: The Gambia operates several sector-specific agricultural information systems, including the Gambia National Agricultural Database, an AfDB-supported Farmer Digitalisation and Farm Registry project, tablet-based farmer registration under the Rice Value Chain Transformation Project, and an e-extension ICT platform developed under the World Bank-funded GIRAV project. These systems operate independently of one another and are not integrated with any national government data exchange or interoperability platform.

Definition: Integration of learner records, academic credentials, enrollment data, and scholarship/bursary systems
Comments: No evidence found of any integration between education systems (learner records, credentials, enrollment) and a national data exchange platform. The Masterplan mentions digital literacy but no specific education system integration plans.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) is outdated. A Memorandum of Understanding signed around 3 July 2026 between the Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education (MoBSE) and the Ministry of Health commits to linking the Education Management Information System (EMIS) with the Health Management Information System (HMIS), with a joint technical working group established to oversee implementation. This is a concrete, dated, sector-specific integration initiative that had not yet begun operating at time of writing. Recoded to 3 (Under development).
revised_comments: The Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education and the Ministry of Health signed a Memorandum of Understanding in July 2026 to link the Education Management Information System with the Health Management Information System, enabling secure data sharing on birth registration, immunisation, nutrition and school enrolment/attendance indicators. A joint technical working group has been established to oversee implementation, though the integration is not yet operational.

Comments: No evidence found of any integration between the electoral register and a national data exchange system. The Independent Electoral Commission manages voter data independently with no documented interoperability plans in current digital strategy documents.

revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) understated available evidence. The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) maintains its own biometric voter register, most recently updated via a March-October 2026 Biometric Voter Registration exercise contracted to Electoral Services International ahead of the December 2026 presidential election. No evidence found that this register is linked to the newly launched National Identity Management System (NIMS, June 2026) or to any cross-government data exchange. Recoded to 1 (Not integrated) on the basis of positive evidence of a standalone system rather than absence of information.
revised_comments: The Independent Electoral Commission maintains an independent biometric voter register, updated through a 2026 Biometric Voter Registration exercise ahead of the December 2026 presidential election. The voter register is managed separately from the country's other identity systems, including the newly launched National Identity Management System, with no documented data-sharing or interoperability arrangement between the two.

Definition: Integration of job seeker registries, unemployment insurance, public employment programs, labor market information
Comments: No evidence found of job seeker registries or labor market systems integrated with any data exchange platform. The Civil Service E-Recruitment Portal is operational but there is no documented interoperability with a national data exchange.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) missed available evidence. The Labour Act 2023 mandates an employment service registry, and the Ministry of Trade, Industry, Regional Integration and Employment has been developing a Labour Market and Migration Information System (LMMIS) linked to five regional job centres. As of April 2026 the Director of Employment describes the LMMIS as linked to job centres but 'not yet fully operational', three years into the policy's implementation. Recoded to 3 (Under development).
revised_comments: The Gambia is developing a Labour Market and Migration Information System, mandated under the Labour Act 2023, intended to link data from five regional job centres to provide real-time employment and labour market information. As of April 2026, officials at the Ministry of Trade, Industry, Regional Integration and Employment describe the system as linked to the job centres but not yet fully operational, with completion targeted for later in 2026.

revised_comments: The Gambian judiciary is digitising internal operations through a Computer-Aided Recording and Transcription System and a planned electronic case management system (the subject of a 2025 UNDP-funded feasibility study), but expansion has been slowed by the suspension of donor funding as of January 2026. These systems remain internal to the judiciary, with no evidence of integration with civil registration, correctional services or a broader government data exchange platform.
